newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk commision rejects Ciller corruption charge.
newsitem.headline: Turk commision rejects Ciller corruption charge.

text.p: A parliamentary commission on Monday rejected a bid to send Turkey's deputy prime minister, Tansu Ciller, to the Supreme Court on corruption charges stemming from her time as head of the government.
"A decision was taken, by 13 votes for and two abstentions, that it was not necessary for Ciller to go to the Supreme Court," commission head Metin Bostancioglu told reporters.

The commission had the remit of deciding whether to ask parliament to send Ciller to the highest court in the land for allegedly failing to prevent contract irregularities at the TEDAS state-run electricity company.
The government had a majority of one MP in the 15-member commission. The TEDAS allegation is the least serious of three corruption charges against Ciller, who is also foreign minister.
She headed three governments from 1993 until earlier this year.
Ciller, a pro-Western secularist, now serves in coalition with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, whose Welfare Party had previously backed the allegations.
